A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same secant-loss research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I. Content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation results, ablations, and training-from-scratch experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds loss-term variability measurements, additional generation results, and a training-efficiency benchmark.

M1.justification: The four secant objectives, EDM/DiT parameterizations, CFG mechanisms and inference procedures are retained. The revised time-sampling setting selects among strategies already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use unconditional CIFAR-10 generation and class-conditional ImageNet-256×256 generation. Additional sampling-step configurations and computational measurements do not introduce new datasets, populations or tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds MeanFlow to the measured efficiency comparison in Table 8 and compares consistency-training and consistency-distillation terms against secant variants in Figure 3. The image-quality comparator sets in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V1 Table 8 becomes v2 Table 9, with CIFAR-10 EMA changed from 0.9999 to 0.99929, horizontal flipping changed from enabled to disabled, and ImageNet STEI time sampling changed from discrete to continuous. Algorithm 7 reflects the latter revision. V2 also introduces timing and memory evaluation at batch size 512 across eight A100 GPUs. These reported setting revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a diagnostic comparing variability of consistency and secant loss terms during training (Figure 3), plus measured computational-efficiency analysis (Appendix G.2). Existing loss-weighting, time-sampling, model-scaling and secant-variant analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 newly reports standard deviations of inspected derivative or target terms at training checkpoints. This adds descriptive variability statistics, not repeated-run uncertainty for benchmark scores. Neither version reports benchmark seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds 1- and 2-step results, although guided ImageNet STEI results at those steps already appeared in v1 Table 3. CIFAR-10 STEI FIDs at 4/8 steps change from 6.32/5.85 to 4.04/2.59; revised settings prevent treating these as matched-protocol gains. Figure 3 adds variability findings, and Table 8 adds timing/memory results. Tables 2–3 retain their scores. Table 8 labels two rows STEI, leaving the final row's method ambiguous.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit STEI and SDEE corollaries with proofs deriving them from existing results; v1 only stated that these cases could be derived. V2 also corrects an algebraic term in Proposition 1 and explicitly states Theorem 3's interval scope. The principal local-convergence framework remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly foreground shared diffusion targets as the reason for training stability. V1's tentative explanation becomes a more definite claim of greater stability than consistency models. The central secant-loss contribution and headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds a target-stability explanation and attributes interior-point variants' advantages to input correctness, error-accumulation paths and capacity used for inversion. It also explicitly distinguishes local theoretical guarantees from bootstrapping to longer intervals. Section 6 retains the same substantive limitations.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promise of future code with a repository link and discloses CFG training ranges in Appendix H. Appendix B.1 corrects the EDM lower time boundary from 0.01 to 0.001, matching the settings table already present in v1. However, Table 7 removes the exact per-row inference guidance scales previously reported.

R1.justification: V2 adds the MeanFlow reference and positions secant losses as an integral counterpart to differentiation-based consistency/MeanFlow objectives under matching parameterizations. The remaining cited works and broad positioning between fast solvers and diffusion distillation are retained.

P1.justification: V2 expands the consistency-model comparison, practical-choice explanation and interpretation of variant performance. It adds acknowledgments and divides Appendix G into performance and efficiency subsections. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the target-stability plot and efficiency table, expands Table 7, and adjusts table formatting and float placement. Existing plots and sample galleries are retained, largely with renumbering; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new stability diagnostic and controlled efficiency benchmark make existing claims more assessable, while explicit corollaries, a code link and CFG training ranges improve completeness. These gains are limited by unexplained setting revisions, removal of exact inference guidance scales, and the duplicated STEI label in Table 8. The additions provide a useful but bounded improvement to an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
